cast.name: Edda Marsh
cast.role: Elder sister, twenty-two. Has run the smallest holding in Ashby Low and raised Wynn since their mother died. The player character on the parish side.
cast.want: To get her sister through this alive, by the rules if there is any way to do it by the rules.
cast.flaw: Obedient. Believes that if you do everything properly, nobody can blame you, and what happens next is not yours.
cast.voice: Practical, clipped, turns every feeling into a chore. 'Eat that. I didn't carry it nine miles to look at it.'
cast.battle: Billhook. Her command is Cover: she takes the hit meant for someone else, and it is almost always the same someone.
cast.secret: She put her own name in the bowl twice that morning, and it still was not her.

cast.name: Wynn Marsh
cast.role: Younger sister, twelve. This year's Demon King.
cast.want: To be good at it. She has been given a part in something the whole parish cares about and means to do it well.
cast.flaw: Wants to please, and cannot tell who is worth pleasing.
cast.voice: Bright, literal, asks what adults step round. 'If it's an honour, why did Mrs Pike cry?'
cast.battle: Begins with Scowl, which does nothing. Her skills arrive on a list the player can read ahead, named in her words: The Loud One, Too Many Stairs, Don't Look.
cast.secret: She can already hear the keep. It sounds like their kitchen.

cast.name: Father Aldous Penhallow
cast.role: Parish priest of Ashby Low. Drew the lot, and travels as chaplain to see the compact properly kept.
cast.want: For it to be done decently and in order.
cast.voice: Gentle, liturgical, all euphemism. 'The incumbent will wish to rest before her installation.'
cast.battle: Rites. Wards the party and, because the compact requires it, blesses the Demon King.
cast.secret: The lot is not drawn blind. The vestry meets the night before. The Marshes have no father and nine acres.

cast.name: Jory Pike
cast.role: The miller's son, nineteen. Volunteered as the Demon King's Guard for the stipend and the hat.
cast.want: To have been part of something.
cast.flaw: Treats it as a festival for longer than anyone should.
cast.voice: Cheerful, loud, narrates himself. 'Jory Pike, Dread Sentinel. That'll look well on a mill.'
cast.battle: Sling and flail. Hits hard, misses often, and gets steadier the worse things become.
cast.secret: His father sits on the vestry. He does not know what that means yet.

cast.name: Isolde 'Izzy' Farrant
cast.role: This generation's Hero, sixteen. A capital foundling chosen by a lottery of her own. The player character on the crown side.
cast.flaw: Believes the story she has been given, completely, because it is the first one that had her in it.
cast.voice: Earnest, self-correcting, trails off. 'I'm the, I'm with Sir Garrick. I'm learning.'
cast.battle: The conventional JRPG lead: sword, a guard stance, a growing list of bright skills that all work best against one large enemy.
cast.secret: Nobody has told her the Demon King is a person from a village. The pictures do not show one.

cast.name: Sir Garrick Lowe
cast.role: The last Hero, fifty-five. Killed the Netherby Demon King thirty years ago and has been dined out on it since. Now Izzy's instructor.
cast.want: To be told by somebody who knows the whole of it that he did right.
cast.flaw: Tells the truth only late at night and only to people who cannot use it.
cast.voice: Dry, tired, north-country. 'There's a plate of me in your church. The engraver added the foot.'
cast.battle: A fading master. Teaches Izzy skills and then, on the day, cannot bring himself to come up the stairs.
cast.secret: At the end the thing went small again, and a man in his shirt asked if he could go home.

cast.name: The Office
cast.role: Whatever lives in the black keep and fills the one who is marked. Not a character so much as a draught.
cast.flaw: It can only use what the person already is.
cast.voice: It has none of its own. In Wynn it sounds like a child being very, very good.
cast.battle: It is the reason monsters rise in a hosting year, and the reason they will not touch her.
cast.secret: No record says what happens to the parishes if it is refused. Every record says what happens if it is fed.

places.name: Ashby Low
places.look: A church, a mill, a green and forty roofs. The lot bowl is the same one used for the harvest pig.
places.play: The opening week: gifts left on the step, the fitting of the horns by the woman who makes the May crown, neighbours who stop meeting your eye.
places.change: If you come back, your nine acres have been ploughed for you. It is meant kindly.

places.name: The Ring Road
places.look: A lane joining the seven parishes in a circle, hedged, with the keep always somewhere on the left.
places.play: The procession. Each parish owes the Demon King a staged tribute and each stretch of road has things that rise in a hosting year, attack the party and kneel to Wynn.
places.change: Walked by both parties at different times. The second to pass finds what the first one left.

places.name: Netherby
places.look: The parish that hosted last time and prospered: new slate, a fat church, a statue of their Demon King with the face chiselled off.
places.play: A tribute scene that turns real when the crowd enjoys itself too much.
places.change: They take the statue down, or put a second one beside it.

places.name: The Hero's Rest
places.look: A coaching inn kept on a crown pension for the use of Heroes, with thirty years of dust on the best room.
places.play: The one place both parties are under a roof together. Played from both sides.
places.change: Its sign shows a knight with his foot on something. By the end someone has painted the something out.

places.name: The Vestry
places.look: A locked room under Ashby church: a century of parish books, and a second, smaller bowl.
places.play: A short investigation dungeon. No monsters. Each ledger read removes an excuse.
places.change: Burned, published, or locked again with you on the right side of the door.

places.name: The Black Keep
places.look: Nobody built it. Inside it becomes whatever the incumbent's mind is like. Wynn's has too many stairs, a kitchen the wrong size, and a room that is entirely the underside of a table.
places.play: Played twice. Edda's party furnishes it, placing the guardians and choosing which doors are locked. Then Izzy's party has to get through what you made.
places.change: At the end it is a hill, or it is occupied.

places.name: The Foundling House
places.look: A tall cold building in the capital with a hundred identical beds and a bowl for who washes up.
places.play: Izzy's opening. A conventional hero's send-off, played completely straight.
places.change: Seen once more in the epilogue, with or without a plate of her on the wall.
